title: Rigidification and coherent enriched-diagram comparison
statement:
Use the universe and infinity-category conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and simplicial model categories and the nerve $N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ as defined in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. For a small simplicial set $K$, let $\mathfrak C[K]$ be the simplicial category obtained by taking the colimit, over the ordinary category of simplices $\Delta^n\to K$, of the simplicial thickenings of $[n]$ defined there. It is left adjoint to $N_{\mathrm{hc}}$. A Dwyer--Kan equivalence of simplicial categories means a simplicial functor inducing weak homotopy equivalences on every mapping simplicial set and an essentially surjective functor on the categories with morphisms $\pi_0$ of those sets.

For every small simplicial category $\mathcal C$ whose mapping simplicial sets are Kan, the counit $\mathfrak C[N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathcal C]\to\mathcal C$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Let $u:\mathfrak C[K]\to\mathcal C$ be a Dwyer--Kan equivalence to a small simplicial category, and let $\mathcal M$ be a combinatorial simplicial model category; combinatorial means locally presentable with both model weak factorization systems generated by small sets, and locally presentable means generated under $\kappa$-filtered colimits, for some regular $\kappa$, by a small set of objects whose Hom functors preserve such colimits. Assume the category $\operatorname{Fun}_{\Delta}(\mathcal C,\mathcal M)$ of simplicial functors is equipped with its simplicial projective model structure (weak equivalences and fibrations are objectwise). There is a categorical equivalence
$$N_{\mathrm{hc}}\bigl(\operatorname{Fun}_{\Delta}(\mathcal C,\mathcal M)^{cf}\bigr)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}\bigl(K,N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal M^{cf})\bigr).$$
It is the comparison induced by enriched evaluation and $u$, so it identifies evaluation at each vertex and the arrows and coherent compositions of diagrams. Universes may be enlarged so that the entire category $\mathcal M$ is available; equivalently one may use the full category as a chunk in the statement of the comparison theorem.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1 (printed p. 89), counit discussed in proof of Corollary 2.2.5.6 (printed p. 93); Example A.3.4.4 and Definition A.3.4.9 (printed pp. 885, 888), which make the full model category a chunk of itself and its projective diagram category; Proposition 4.2.4.4 and Remark 4.2.4.5 (printed p. 258), allowing the full chunk after universe enlargement. Read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this theorem.
